lede: Gold fell about 3.6% on Friday to near $3,876, its lowest level in a year, as bets on a December Fed hike and a tech-led stock selloff forced investors to sell. Forex and gold are closed until Monday; next week brings the US midterms, the BoE decision and Friday's payrolls.

focus.text: Broke below $4,000 and closed the week down about 3.7%. It sits under Monday's pivot of 3,924.5; Friday's low near 3,870 is the nearest reference.
Ended October more than 1% lower, near its weakest in over a year, on French fiscal worries and weak growth. Eurozone CPI on Wednesday and US payrolls on Friday are the key tests.

news.text: The Fed held at 3.75–4.00% this week but two members voted for a hike; futures now price roughly a 76% chance of a December increase.
Most Wall Street analysts in Kitco's weekly survey expect further losses next week, while retail voters remain mostly bullish.
Brent climbed above $113 after a tanker was struck by limpet mines in the Strait of Hormuz, adding to inflation concerns.
Bitcoin hit a six-week low after a $6.3B Binance hack; the exchange plans phased withdrawals and proof-of-reserves data by Monday.
Sterling is near its strongest since mid-September as markets almost fully price a Bank of England hike on 5 November.
